spots.name: Kremlin

hours.note: Closed Thu

spots.summary: The Moscow Kremlin, commonly known as the Kremlin, is a fortified complex (kremlin) in Moscow, Russia. Located in the historic centre of the country's capital city, the Kremlin comprises five palaces, four cathedrals, and an enclosing wall along with numerous towers.

spots.name: Red Square
spots.summary: Red Square is one of the oldest and largest squares in Moscow, Russia. It is in Moscow's historic centre, along the eastern walls of the Kremlin. It is the city's most prominent landmark, with famous buildings such as Saint Basil's Cathedral, Lenin's Mausoleum, the State Historical Museum and the GUM department store.

spots.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Vasily the Blessed, commonly known as Saint Basil's Cathedral, is a Russian Orthodox church on Red Square in the historic centre of Moscow. It is one of the most popular cultural symbols of Russia.

spots.name: Lenin's Mausoleum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Fri

spots.summary: Lenin's Mausoleum, also known as Lenin's Tomb, is a mausoleum located at Red Square in Moscow, Russia. It serves as the resting place of Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin, whose preserved body has been on public display since shortly after his death in 1924, with rare exceptions in wartime.

spots.name: Kremlin Wall Necropolis
spots.summary: The Kremlin Wall Necropolis is the former national cemetery of the Soviet Union, located in Red Square in Moscow beside the Kremlin Wall. Burials there began in November 1917, when 240 pro-Bolsheviks who died during the Moscow Bolshevik Uprising were buried in mass graves.

spots.name: Seven Sisters

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Seven Sisters are a group of seven skyscrapers in Moscow designed in the Stalinist style, also known as Stalinist "Empire style". They were built from 1947 to 1957.

spots.name: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Christ the Saviour is a Russian Orthodox cathedral in Moscow, Russia, on the northern bank of the Moskva River, a few hundred metres southwest of the Kremlin. With an overall height of 103 metres (338 ft), it is the third tallest Orthodox Christian church building in the world.

spots.name: Cathedral of the Archangel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Archangel is a Russian Orthodox church dedicated to the Archangel Michael. It is located in Cathedral Square of the Moscow Kremlin in Russia between the Great Kremlin Palace and the Ivan the Great Bell Tower.

spots.name: Novodevichy Cemetery
spots.summary: Novodevichy Cemetery is a cemetery in Moscow, Russia. It lies next to the southern wall of the 16th-century Novodevichy Convent.

spots.name: Lubyanka Building
spots.summary: Lubyanka is the popular name for the building which contains the headquarters of the FSB on Lubyanka Square in the Meshchansky District of Moscow, Russia. It is a large Neo-Baroque building with a facade of yellow brick designed by Alexander V. Ivanov in 1897 and augmented by Aleksey Shchusev from 1940 to 1947.

spots.name: Tretyakov Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The State Tretyakov Gallery is an art gallery in Moscow, Russia, which is considered the foremost depository of Russian fine art in the world.

spots.name: Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy
spots.summary: Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy is a permanent general purpose trade show and amusement park in Moscow, Russia. Between 1991 and 2014, it was also called the All-Russia Exhibition Centre. It is a state joint-stock company.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy

spots.name: Moscow International Business Center
spots.summary: The Moscow International Business Center (MIBC), also known as Moscow-City, is an under-construction commercial development in Moscow, the capital of Russia.

spots.name: Tsar Cannon
spots.summary: The Tsar Cannon is a large early modern period artillery piece on display on the grounds of the Moscow Kremlin. It is a monument of Russian artillery casting art, cast in bronze in 1586 in Moscow, by the Russian master bronze caster Andrey Chokhov. Mostly of symbolic impact, it was never used in a war.

spots.name: Dormition Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Dormition, also known as the Assumption Cathedral or Cathedral of the Assumption, is a Russian Orthodox church dedicated to the Dormition of the Theotokos.

spots.name: Main building of Moscow State University

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The main building of Moscow State University is a 239-metre (784 ft), 36-story skyscraper in Moscow, Russia. It was designed by Lev Rudnev as the headquarters of Moscow State University, and is the tallest among the "Seven Sisters" constructed in Moscow between 1947 and 1953 in the Stalinist architectural style.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Main building of Moscow State University

spots.name: Tsar Bell
spots.summary: The Tsar Bell, also known as the Tsarsky Kolokol, Tsar Kolokol III, or Royal Bell, is a 6.14-metre-tall (20.1 ft), 6.6-metre-diameter (22 ft) bell on display on the grounds of the Moscow Kremlin. The bell was commissioned by Empress Anna Ivanovna, niece of Peter the Great.

spots.name: Grand Kremlin Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grand Kremlin Palace is a building in the Moscow Kremlin. For much of the 19th century, it served as the official residence of the Russian emperor in Moscow, which was not then the capital of the Russian Empire.

spots.name: Pushkin Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts is the largest museum of European art in Moscow. It is located in Volkhonka street, just opposite the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour. The International musical festival Sviatoslav Richter's December Nights has been held in the Pushkin Museum since 1981.

spots.name: Novodevichy Convent
spots.summary: Novodevichy Convent, also known as Bogoroditse-Smolensky Monastery, is probably the best-known cloister of Moscow. Its name, sometimes translated as the New Maidens' Monastery, was devised to differ from the Old Maidens' Monastery within the Moscow Kremlin.

spots.name: GUM
spots.summary: GUM is a shopping center in Moscow, Russia. It was also the main department store in many cities of the former Soviet Union; similarly named stores operated in some Soviet republics and in post-Soviet states.

spots.name: Worker and Kolkhoz Woman
spots.summary: Worker and Kolkhoz Woman is a sculpture of two figures with a hammer and a sickle raised over their heads. The concept and compositional design belong to the Soviet architect Boris Iofan.

spots.name: Hotel Ukraina, Moscow
spots.summary: Hotel Ukraina, also known as the Radisson Collection Hotel, Moscow, is a five-star luxury hotel in Moscow, situated on a bend of the Moskva River. The hotel is one of the "Seven Sisters", a group of Stalin-era skyscrapers of Moscow, and stands 206 metres (676 ft) tall.

spots.name: Spasskaya Tower
spots.summary: The Spasskaya Tower, also translated as the Saviour Tower, is the main tower on the eastern wall of the Moscow Kremlin which overlooks Red Square.

spots.name: Bolshoi Theatre
spots.summary: The Bolshoi Theatre is a historic opera house in Moscow, Russia, originally designed by architect Joseph Bové. Before the October Revolution it was a part of the Imperial Theatres of the Russian Empire along with Maly Theatre in Moscow and a few theatres in Saint Petersburg.

spots.name: Kotelnicheskaya Embankment Building
spots.summary: Kotelnicheskaya Embankment Building is one of seven Stalinist skyscrapers laid down in September 1947 and completed in 1952, designed by Dmitry Chechulin and Andrei Rostkovsky. The main tower has 32 levels and is 176 metres (577 ft) tall. At the time of construction it was the tallest building in Europe.

spots.name: Monument to Minin and Pozharsky
spots.summary: The Monument to Minin and Pozharsky is a bronze statue designed by Ivan Martos and located on the Red Square in Moscow, Russia, in front of Saint Basil's Cathedral.

spots.name: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
spots.summary: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is a war memorial in the Alexander Garden in Moscow near the Kremlin dedicated to the Soviet soldiers killed during World War II. It was designed by architects D. I. Burdin, V. A. Klimov, Yu. R. Rabayev and sculptor Nikolai Tomsky.

spots.name: Ivan the Great Bell Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ivan the Great Bell Tower is a church tower inside the Moscow Kremlin complex. With a total height of 81 metres (266 ft), it is the tallest tower and structure of the Kremlin.

spots.name: Kazan Cathedral
spots.summary: Kazan Cathedral, formally known as the "Cathedral of Our Lady of Kazan", is a Russian Orthodox church located on the northwest corner of Red Square in Moscow, Russia. The current building is a reconstruction of the original church, which was destroyed on the orders of Joseph Stalin in 1936.

spots.name: Kolomenskoye

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Kolomenskoye is a former royal estate situated several kilometers to the southeast of the city center of Moscow, Russia, on the ancient road leading to the town of Kolomna. The 390 hectare scenic area overlooks the steep banks of the Moskva River. It became a part of Moscow in the 1960s.

spots.name: Moscow Zoo

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Moscow Zoo or Moskovsky Zoopark is a 21.5-hectare (53-acre) zoo, one of the largest in Russia and one of the oldest in Europe.

spots.name: State Kremlin Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The State Kremlin Palace, previously and unofficially known as the Kremlin Palace of Congresses, is a large modern building inside the Moscow Kremlin.

spots.name: Maly Theatre

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Maly Theatre is a theatre in Moscow, Russia, principally associated with the production of plays. Established in 1806 and operating on its present site on the Theatre Square since 1824, the theatre traces its history to the Moscow University drama company, established in 1756.

spots.name: Ostankino Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ostankino Tower is a television and radio tower in Moscow, Russia, owned by the Moscow branch of unitary enterprise Russian TV and Radio Broadcasting Network. Standing 540.1 metres (1,772 ft), it was designed by Nikolai Nikitin.

spots.name: Kremlin Senate

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kremlin Senate is a building within the grounds of the Moscow Kremlin in Russia. Initially constructed from 1776 to 1787, it originally housed the Moscow branch of the Governing Senate, the highest judiciary and legislative office of Imperial Russia.

spots.name: Leningradsky railway station
spots.summary: Moscow Leningradsky railway station is the oldest of Moscow's ten railway terminals. Situated on Komsomolskaya Square, the station serves north-western directions, notably Saint Petersburg. International services from the station include Tallinn, Estonia, operated by GoRail, and Helsinki, Finland.

spots.name: Lubyanka Square
spots.summary: Lubyanskaya Square, or simply Lubyanka in Moscow lies about 900 metres (980 yd) north-east of Red Square. History first records its name in 1480, when Grand Prince Ivan III of Moscow, who had conquered Novgorod in 1471, settled many Novgorodians in the area.

spots.name: State Historical Museum
spots.summary: The State Historical Museum of Russia is a museum of Russian history located between Red Square and Manege Square in Moscow. The museum's exhibitions range from relics of prehistoric tribes that lived in the territory of present-day Russia, to priceless artworks acquired by members of the Romanov dynasty.

spots.name: Okhotny Ryad
spots.summary: Okhotny Ryad is a station on the Sokolnicheskaya Line of the Moscow Metro. It is situated in the very centre of Moscow in the Tverskoy District, near the Kremlin, Manezhnaya Square and State Duma. It is named after a nearby street, whose name literally means "hunters' row".

spots.name: Gorky Park
spots.summary: Gorky Central Park of Culture and Leisure is a central park in Moscow, named after Maxim Gorky. In August 2018, the Park's 90th anniversary was celebrated.

spots.name: House on the Embankment
spots.summary: The House on the Embankment is a block-wide apartment building on the banks of the Moskva River on Balchug in downtown Moscow, Russia. It faces Bersenevskaya Embankment on one side and Serafimovicha Street on the other side. Until 1952, it was the tallest residential building in Moscow.

spots.name: Lubyanka
spots.summary: Lubyanka is a station on the Sokolnicheskaya Line of the Moscow Metro, located under Lubyanka Square. The facility, originally called Dzerzhinskaya station, opened in 1935 as part of the first stage of the metro.

spots.name: Ploshchad Revolyutsii
spots.summary: Ploshchad Revolyutsii is a station of the Moscow Metro system, in the Tverskoy District of central Moscow, Russia. The station is on the Arbatsko-Pokrovskaya Line and named after Revolution Square, under which it is located.

spots.name: Cathedral of the Annunciation

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Annunciation in Moscow is a Russian Orthodox church dedicated to the Annunciation of the Theotokos.

spots.name: Moscow Kiyevsky railway station
spots.summary: Kiyevsky railway terminal also known as Moscow Kiyevskaya railway station is one of the nine railway terminals of Moscow, Russia. It is the only railway station in Moscow to have a frontage on the Moskva River.

spots.name: Shukhov Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Shukhov Radio Tower, also known as the Shabolovka Tower, is a broadcasting tower deriving from the Russian avant-garde in Moscow designed by Vladimir Shukhov. The 160-metre-high (520 ft) free-standing steel diagrid structure was built between 1920 and 1922, during the Russian Civil War.

spots.name: Federation Tower
spots.summary: The Federation Tower is a complex of two skyscrapers built on the 13th lot of the Moscow International Business Center in Moscow, Russia. The two skyscrapers are named Tower East or Vostok and Tower West or Zapad.

spots.name: Palace of Facets

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of the Facets is a building in the Moscow Kremlin, Russia, which contains what used to be the main banquet reception hall of the Russian tsars. It is the oldest preserved secular building in Moscow. Located on Kremlin Cathedral Square, between the Cathedral of the Annunciation and the Dormition Cathedral.

spots.name: Donskoy Monastery

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Donskoy Monastery is a major monastery in Moscow, founded in 1591 in commemoration of Moscow's deliverance from the threat of an invasion by the Crimean Khan Kazy-Girey. Commanding a highway to the Crimea, the monastery was intended to defend southern approaches to the Moscow Kremlin.

spots.name: VDNKh
spots.summary: VDNKh is a Moscow Metro station in Ostankinsky District, North-Eastern Administrative Okrug, Moscow, Russia. It is located on the Kaluzhsko-Rizhskaya Line, between Alekseyevskaya and Botanichesky Sad stations. VDNKh was opened on 1 May 1958.

spots.name: Manezhnaya Square
spots.summary: Manezhnaya is a pedestrian open space in the Tverskoy District, at the heart of Moscow. It is bound by the Hotel Moskva to the east, the State Historical Museum and the Alexander Garden to the south, the Moscow Manege to the west, and the 18th-century headquarters of the Moscow State University to the north.

spots.name: Zaryadye Park
spots.summary: Zaryadye Park is a landscape urban park located adjacent to Red Square in Moscow, Russia, on the site of the former Zaryadye district. The park was inaugurated on 9 September 2017 by Russian president Vladimir Putin and Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin.

spots.name: Russian Institute of Theatre Arts
spots.summary: The Russian Institute of Theatre Arts (GITIS) is the largest and oldest independent theatrical arts school in Russia. Located in Moscow, the school was founded on 22 September 1878 as the Shostakovsky Music School.

spots.name: Vvedenskoye Cemetery
spots.summary: Vvedenskoye Cemetery is a historic cemetery in Lefortovo District of Moscow in Russia.

spots.name: Vagankovo Cemetery
spots.summary: Vagankovo Cemetery is located in the Presnensky District of Moscow, Russia. It was established in 1771, in an effort to curb an outbreak of bubonic plague in Central Russia. The cemetery was one of those created outside the city proper so as to prevent the contagion from spreading.

spots.name: Mayakovskaya
spots.summary: Mayakovskaya is a Moscow Metro station on the Zamoskvoretskaya Line, in the Tverskoy District of central Moscow, Russia.

spots.name: Moscow Conservatory
spots.summary: The Moscow Conservatory, also officially Tchaikovsky Moscow State Conservatory is a higher musical educational institution located in Moscow, Russia. It grants undergraduate and graduate degrees in musical performance and musical research.

spots.name: Lobnoye Mesto
spots.summary: Lobnoye mesto is a 13-meter-long stone platform situated in the Red Square in Moscow in front of Saint Basil's Cathedral.

spots.name: Moscow Belorussky railway station
spots.summary: Belorussky railway station also referred to as Moscow–Passenger–Smolenskaya, Informally the whole station can be called as Moscow Belorusskaya, is a railway terminal of the Moscow Railway located at the front of Tverskaya Zastava Square in Central Administrative Okrug, Moscow.

spots.name: Taynitsky Garden
spots.summary: This is an urban park at the southern walls of the Moscow Kremlin. One highlight of this garden was an oak tree named Cosmos, planted by Yuri Gagarin on 14 Apr 1961, just two days after his return from his historic space flight.

spots.name: Tverskaya Street
spots.summary: This road was a very important thoroughfare in Tsarist Russia. It is now Moscow's most fashionable street, with several prestigious boutiques. It is also lined with cafés, restaurants, coffeehouses, a couple of theatres, and several hotels, including two locations of the Marriott. spots.name: Vysokopetrovsky Monastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Russian Orthodox monastery. Founded in the 1320s. In the late 17th century, the Naryshkin boyars, maternal relatives of Peter the Great, turned the monastery into their family burial place. They had it reconstructed in the Naryshkin Baroque style of architecture. In the mid-18th century, several subsidiary structures were added. Now here find you the Moscow Literature Museum.

spots.summary: A large Russian Orthodox convent in central Moscow. It is the main shrine of St. John the Baptist in the Russian capital.
